newsitem.title: FINLAND: Metra's Wartsila sees growth in Africa.
newsitem.headline: Metra's Wartsila sees growth in Africa.

text.p: Finnish engineering group Metra Oy Ab's Wartsila NSD unit sees prospects for sustained growth in power plant sales to Africa, a senior Wartsila NSD executive said on Wednesday.
Wartsila earlier announced a 580 million markka ($114 million) order from Tanzanian Independent Power Tanzania Ltd (IPTL), which it said would be an important reference in Africa.
"In three to six years, it should be possible to achieve sales of $200 million per year to the African continent," Wartsila NSD Nederland president Albert Dragt told Reuters.

Up to now, the group's engine sales to African countries have been under $100 million per year, Dragt said, but added that average annual African sales of $100 million and above should be sustainable on a three- to five-year horizon.
"This is not a breakthrough," Dragt said of the Tanzanian order for 10 engines, "but it is a step ahead in African power plant investment."

"We are focusing on developing countries and developing markets where there is growing demand for energy, and that is mainly in Asia and Latin America -- and now, coming up, the African market," Dragt said.
In 1996, Asia accounted over half of the group's total power plant deliveries and Europe for 20 percent.
Wartsila NSD was created at the beginning of this year through the merger of Metra's Wartsila Diesel and Swiss engine builder New Sulzer Diesel.
In January-April, Wartsila NSD's net sales rose 42 percent to 2.6 billion markka from 1.9 billion a year ago, with the newly merged units generating 0.5 billion markka of the total.
Wartsila Diesel's full-year 1996 net sales were 8.0 billion markka, up 16 percent on 1995. Power plant sales accounted for 49 percent of the 1996 total.
Wartsila NSD expects group net sales to exceed 11 billion markka this year, it said, repeating an earlier sales forecast.
